ops.title: A green -race run does not prove a t.Parallel sweep is safe
ops.body:
PR #77 (3fe5f60) added 137 t.Parallel() calls to internal/cli in one sweep. Four turned
out to be unsafe. Three of the four were INVISIBLE to `go test -race`:

1. TestVersionPrintsBareTag wrote the package global internal/version.Version, read by
   every sibling through NewRootCmd -> version.String(). This one DID fire (~25 tests).
   Fixed upstream in c661f4d (#90).
2. TestPruneRepairsAStackOverAForgottenParent wrote the package var cli.gtAPIClient via
   stubGTAPI. Silent because every other reader of that var was serial.
3. TestShowLiveSmoke called a process-wide os.Chdir. Silent because it t.Skips before the
   chdir unless CCX_LIVE_SMOKE=1.
4. TestReadCommandNamesNoRoot called workspace.SetRoot, a process-wide pin. Silent because
   the pin is RWMutex-guarded - no race, just the wrong answer. 77 of the 137 statically
   reach a root read. Fixed in #124.

So a green -race run is NOT evidence that a parallel sweep is safe. It proves only that
nothing raced on that schedule, and says nothing about mutex-guarded shared state, or
about a hazard whose only conflicting reader happens to be serial today.

What does work, and is cheap: enumerate rather than search. Build a type-checked
cross-package call graph (go/packages) and compute, per parallel test, the reachable set
of functions that write package-scope state or call raw os.Setenv/Chdir/Unsetenv.
Repo-wide that writer set is 14 named functions, none an interface method - which is what
bounds the claim, since imprecise dispatch cannot then hide one from direct-call analysis.
Run a positive control: re-introduce a known hazard and confirm the analyzer flags it.

Verdict: of the 136 still-live calls, 28 reach no shared-state writer, 106 reach only
mutex-guarded deterministic memoizers (vcstest templates/hosts, rank patterns,
dispatch/web embedders, engine residentIndex, format engineInst), and the only sharp roots
were the known ones. Wrong only if a hazard reaches shared state through unsafe,
reflection, or a cgo/subprocess path the call graph does not model.
